title: In a Harvard physics course, median learning gains with an AI tutor were more than double those of an active-learning class
summary: Harvard students who used PS2 Pal, powered by GPT-4-0613, learned more in less time than students in an active-learning class.
account: In autumn 2023 the course team of Harvard University's Physical Sciences 2 ran a randomized controlled crossover experiment with 194 students. The paper places the study in “the Fall 2023 semester” and its lessons in “the ninth and tenth weeks of the course”, later in the term, without a calendar date. It covered two topics, surface tension and fluid flow. Each student learned one topic in an in-class active-learning session and the other at home with a purpose-built AI tutor. The supplement identifies the tutor as PS2 Pal, built in TeachGPT and powered by GPT-4-0613. Instructors supplied the solutions and teaching prompts. Harvard reported on 5 September 2024 that colleagues were trying the tutor framework and that Math 21a and the Derek Bok Center would pilot similar tutors that fall. The Hechinger Report noted on 16 September 2024 that the at-home sessions were proctored over Zoom and questioned whether students would use the tutor on their own. The paper was published in Scientific Reports on 3 June 2025. The authors report that “students learn significantly more in less time when using the AI tutor”. They report median learning gains over double those of the class session, with a median of 49 minutes on task, and higher engagement and motivation.
purpose: The tutor was built to teach these physics lessons with research-based pedagogy. The learning gain is the result that it was built to produce.
system: PS2 Pal, Harvard’s physics tutor built in TeachGPT using GPT-4-0613
developer: Harvard University (Kestin, Miller, Klales, Milbourne, Ponti)

fields.summary: Harvard students who used PS2 Pal, powered by GPT-4-0613, learned more in less time than students in an active-learning class.
fields.account: In autumn 2023 the course team of Harvard University's Physical Sciences 2 ran a randomized controlled crossover experiment with 194 students. The paper places the study in “the Fall 2023 semester” and its lessons in “the ninth and tenth weeks of the course”, later in the term, without a calendar date. It covered two topics, surface tension and fluid flow. Each student learned one topic in an in-class active-learning session and the other at home with a purpose-built AI tutor. The supplement identifies the tutor as PS2 Pal, built in TeachGPT and powered by GPT-4-0613. Instructors supplied the solutions and teaching prompts. Harvard reported on 5 September 2024 that colleagues were trying the tutor framework and that Math 21a and the Derek Bok Center would pilot similar tutors that fall. The Hechinger Report noted on 16 September 2024 that the at-home sessions were proctored over Zoom and questioned whether students would use the tutor on their own. The paper was published in Scientific Reports on 3 June 2025. The authors report that “students learn significantly more in less time when using the AI tutor”. They report median learning gains over double those of the class session, with a median of 49 minutes on task, and higher engagement and motivation.
